pr_body:
Currently the `fields` API fetches the root flattened field and returns it in a
structured way in the response. In addition this change makes it possible to
directly query subfields. However, requesting flattened subfields via wildcard
patterns is not possible.

Closes #70605
pr_comment: @jtibshirani thanks, I think I adressed your change requests and added a unit and a yaml test. I think I will also add a short passage to the docs somewhere about fetching flattened subfields and that the naming has to be exact, I haven't found a good spot yet though. Will be back with another short update shortly.

review_comment: I just realized we should throw an error if the format is non-null, as we do for most other field types. (This is unfortunately very manual right now and easy to forget...)
It'd be nice to add a unit test here -- we've been adding tests like `RootFlattenedFieldTypeTests#testFetchSourceValue` for all the field type that support fetching.

I'm not entirely sure if this gets in the way of other logic, but in the case of a flattened subfield we would return the root path otherwise without this extra step before the rest of the logic here. Happy to hear if there are better places to but this overwrite.
I think this is correct, it's the only way to distinguish between a flattened field and a multifield.
